rows.evidence: org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[[]]> but was:<[[x-i̇d raw=[v] headers=[]]]>
rows.note: A header name containing U+0130 (capital dotted I), sent through the in-memory adapter, appears in headerNames() as 'x-i̇d' (Locale.ROOT lowercase gives two chars: i plus a combining dot). req.headers('x-i̇d') returns [] because String.equalsIgnoreCase compares char by char, and the string lengths differ. So for this name of headerNames(), req.headers(name) does not give its raw values. Fix: match headerNames() against headers() using one rule, either a per-char case fold or toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) equality. Reach: TinyHttpd cannot hit this because it decodes header names as ISO-8859-1; the in-memory adapter can, and so can any adapter that decodes header names as UTF-8.

rows.evidence: org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[x-[a, x-b]]|[1, 2]|[1, 2, 3]|n...> but was:<[x-[b, x-a]]|[1, 2]|[1, 2, 3]|n...>
rows.note: On embedded Jetty 9.4, headerNames() gives [x-b, x-a], not the [x-a, x-b] that PRD-181 (AC-A4 servlet half) states. The values (1, 2, 3; x-a = 1, 2) and the unmodifiability are correct. Not kept for wave-3: DefaultRequest faithfully reports the order the adapter gives, as FR-HTTP-032 requires; the servlet half of PRD-181 belongs to FR-SVL-010 AC-1 (wave-9). Signal for wave-9: Jetty's getHeaderNames order comes from a hash set, so FR-SVL-010 AC-1 ([x-a, x-b]) and FR-SVL-010 AC-2 (names follow the container's enumeration order) cannot both hold with the current ServletExchange.snapshotHeaders.
Jetty loopback peer inside trustProxyCidrs(127.0.0.0/8, ::1/128): true and remoteAddress follows X-Forwarded-For.
